title: RC-25 no newer-schema guard: importing db.ts migrates and then writes user_version = 7 unconditionally, so an older build opened on a newer database silently downgrades its version, and every import (including the read-only preflight command) writes the live database

evidence.note: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 7; version read with no upper-bound check
db.pragma(`user_version = ${CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION}`) runs on every import, whatever version was found
new Database(DB_PATH) (creates the file if missing), then WAL and synchronous pragmas, all at import
normalizeLegacyMainnetRows runs an UPDATE on every import
all prepared statements are compiled at import against whatever schema is on disk
the preflight module imports './utils/db', so any process that loads preflight opens, migrates and writes the database

sibling_sites_checked: The forensic copy showed 40 page-1 header writes with user_version 7 and no row changes, the fingerprint of this import path (AUD-FORENSIC-001, AUD-RAIL-002; linked, not repeated). scripts/preflight.ts and scripts/pause.ts / resume.ts (SCRIPTS slice) load db.ts the same way. The 22-09 rail (D-08, D-24) adds a read-only version probe before any pragma and refuses a CURRENT+1 database; 22-29 re-audits that diff.
severity_rationale: S2, equal to the research suggestion. Effects of an older build on a newer database: user_version drops to 7, so the next newer boot re-runs its migrations (a non-idempotent ALTER then fails and the bot cannot boot); a removed column makes a prepared statement fail at import (refuses to start); a newly required column makes the buy-row insert fail after the buy has landed (stranded position). Needs a rollback to an older build after a schema change, which D-ROLLBACK makes plausible but not routine. Mitigated by the 22-09 rail; status stays confirmed until 22-29 verifies it.
recommendation: Mitigated by the planned 22-09 rail (read-only user_version probe before any write; refuse version > CURRENT with the file hash unchanged). 22-29 re-audits the db.ts diff; no further behaviour decision.

sub_claims.claim: user_version is written unconditionally, downgrading a newer database
Prepared statements compiled at import assume the schema-7 columns
Every import of db.ts writes the database (pragma user_version and an UPDATE), including the read-only preflight command

fix_scope: Closes the newer-schema half only: a database at a higher version is refused with its bytes unchanged. The other half of the title, that every import of db.ts writes the database (the unconditional user_version write and the normalizeLegacyMainnetRows update), is not changed by the rail, so the status stays confirmed. Phase 24 decides whether import-time writes change.

triage.note: Open half reproduced (AC-14, plan 23-13): every import of src/utils/db.ts writes the database. A railed child (VITEST unset, so the production branch runs; DB_PATH a temp file; a throwaway working folder) that only imports src/utils/db on an up-to-date WAL database built by the real migrations commits one write: PRAGMA data_version on the test's own held connection moves, a SHA-256 over the main file plus its -wal changes, and wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) reports 1 WAL frame (claim import-writes-database, observed {committedWrite true, databaseBytesChanged true, walFrames 1}, correct {false, false, 0}). The write is the unconditional PRAGMA user_version = 7 at the end of migrateSchema (src/utils/dbSchema.ts); the normalizeLegacyMainnetRows UPDATE matches no row and commits nothing, and a pragmas-only control (the journal_mode, synchronous and busy_timeout pragmas db.ts issues, no migration) commits nothing. The main file alone does not change until a checkpoint (a child that exits without closeDb, beside a held connection, runs none), so a main-file hash would miss the write. The newer-schema half is closed by the 22-09 rail: 'AC-24 schema version guard > a v8 database (CURRENT+1) refuses and its bytes are unchanged' in test/integration/dbGuards.test.ts (RED proof row 11). Phase 24 reading: writing user_version only when it differs flips the claim to looks fixed (fix-shaped mutation of dbSchema.ts, src restored byte for byte).
